title: In-Memory Unix File System
prompt:
Build an in-memory Unix-style file system for absolute paths such as /, /var, and /var/log.txt. Repeated slashes and a trailing slash normalize to the same location, so /x///y/ means /x/y.

Implement InMemoryUnixFileSystem with these methods:
- touch(path): create an empty file when its parent directory already exists. Calling touch on an existing file is a no-op. Raise ValueError when the path is root, the parent is absent, or the name already identifies a directory.
- mkdir(path): create a directory with mkdir -p semantics. Missing directories along the path are created; an existing directory is a no-op. Raise ValueError if a path component names a file.
- ls(path): return a directory's child names in lexicographic order. When path is a file, return a one-item list containing that file name.
- rm(path): remove a file and return True. Return False for root, a missing path, or a directory.
- rmdir(path): remove an empty non-root directory and return True. Return False for root, a missing path, a file, or a nonempty directory.

A file and directory may not share a name in the same parent. All paths passed to the API are absolute.

example.reasoning: mkdir creates missing ancestors, while ls lists both the file and directory in lexical order.
